judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Deemed properly given when delivered" covers personal, fax, courier and mail alike without saying when mailed notice is deemed delivered, and the address block gives no address for Ajuba India even though Ajuba India owes most of the payment obligations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Notices to "the Company or the Board" go to a single Michigan address although the preamble defines Company to include the Indian entity and 8.5 requires notice to "the Company"; the mismatch is real but unlikely to be decisive.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence withholding provision with no ambiguity in its terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contemplates only "federal, state and local" taxes although the Employee is required by 8.2(d) to reside in India and is paid by Ajuba India — Indian withholding is unaddressed, a gap rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The ongoing provisions of this Agreement, which shall survive... in accordance with their terms" never identifies which provisions are ongoing — a circular survival clause that names nothing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether Articles III, IV and V survive termination matters enormously given the Restricted Period runs three years past the Employment Term, and this clause supplies no list to check them against; that indeterminacy is a whole-instrument problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The integration clause carves out "that certain Non-Competition Agreement of even date herewith," an unattached instrument, leaving the relationship between two contemporaneous non-compete regimes unstated on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article V of this Agreement itself contains full noncompetition covenants, so the carve-out means two overlapping restraints of unknown relative scope govern the same conduct; 6.1's representation that the Employee is not subject to any other non-compete adds to the strain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The Parties" is capitalised but never defined in this Agreement (only in Exhibit A), and the clause both denies and then confers third-party beneficiary status on Parent without saying which rights Parent may enforce.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parent is given substantive protection in 1.5, 1.7 and Article V(b) yet is a non-signatory, so what Parent may enforce and against whom has to be worked out across those provisions and this one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional Michigan choice-of-law clause excluding renvoi; the words themselves are plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies Michigan law to an employment relationship required by 8.2(d) to be performed in India by an Indian employer, which invites argument about mandatory foreign employment law; Exhibit A ¶17 repeats the same choice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure boilerplate with no interpretive content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the duplicate signature pages appended to the document; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Except as may be contrary to applicable law" is a soft opener, but the prohibition on alienation of benefits is otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.4 makes the Agreement bind and benefit the Employee's "heirs... and personal representatives," and 8.3 contemplates payments involving his estate, which sits slightly against a blanket bar on transfer of benefits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Disparage" is undefined and the obligation is perpetual ("and thereafter") with no carve-out for truthful statements or compelled testimony; the sentence also ends without punctuation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A ¶3 states the non-disparagement obligation quite differently — limited to "so long as Employee holds Restricted Stock Units," with express exceptions — so the two non-disparagement regimes in the same instrument do not match.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, clear recusal undertaking; "that portion of the meeting" is readily applied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Board" is defined as Ajuba's board, while 8.4(b) speaks of Parent removing the Employee from the Board and 2.1 lets him report to a designee of Parent's board — the recusal duty is coherent but the Board references across the instrument are loose.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "May be brought against any of parties in the courts of the State of Michigan" is permissive on its face and omits a word ("any of [the] parties"), so whether it is an exclusive forum selection or a mere consent to jurisdiction is genuinely contestable — precisely the mandatory/permissive fight that clauses like this generate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the Agreement addresses forum, though the clause has to work alongside 9.10's Michigan choice of law and a wholly India-based employment relationship; no contradiction, but real interpretive work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital block is riddled with blanks and garbled text ("OF Employee has been given...", "eis consideration of the foregoing"), with recital C effectively swallowed into B and no date filled in for either the Employment Agreement or the termination.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Recital D says the parties wish to release "any and all claims and demands asserted or which could be asserted," while operative ¶1 expressly excludes claims to compel payment of amounts due under the Employment Agreement — a recital pointing further than the operative text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long omnibus release built on "including, but not limited to" lists, whose only carve-out — claims "to compel the payment of amounts due to Employee as provided in the Employment Agreement" — is narrow and its boundary against, say, bonus disputes is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The release is the condition of severance under 8.4, yet it purports to release claims "which occurred up to the date of this Agreement" while preserving payment claims that will accrue after it; reconciling the release with the continuing severance stream in 8.4 takes some work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A very broad but enumerated return-of-property obligation defined as "Company Information and Property"; the words are clear even if the list is sweeping.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates 3.2 and 4.2 with a third, differently defined category of returnable material, so three overlapping definitions govern the same conduct; overlap rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The duration trigger — "[f]or so long as Employee holds Restricted Stock Units" — depends on an instrument nowhere mentioned in this Agreement, and the clause refers to "the circumstances of Employee's resignation" although the Release is used for company-initiated terminations too.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.13 imposes a mutual, perpetual non-disparagement obligation "[d]uring the Employment Term and thereafter"; this paragraph makes the Employee's obligation contingent on holding RSUs, so the two provisions cannot both be given full effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "To never seek or accept employment with Company" is a subjectless fragment — the paragraph has no operative subject or verb tying the promise to the Employee — and the waiver of "any claim in connection with any future refusal by the Company to employ him" is very broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside ¶1's release of employment-discrimination claims and is in tension with the perpetual, unqualified nature of the promise given Article V's restraints are time-limited; the fit is loose but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short acknowledgment that specified Employment Agreement obligations continue; clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves "non-competition and restricted business activities" obligations while V(d) narrows them to Core Business on an 8.4 termination — and this Release is signed only on an 8.4 termination — so the interaction between the two is worth construing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Upon reasonable notice" and "a reasonable amount of the Employee's time" are soft, but they are the ordinary and workable formulation for a cooperation covenant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Company's promise to reimburse "lost wages" fits awkwardly with ¶4's bar on any future employment relationship, but nothing squarely conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple factual acknowledgment with a cross-reference to paragraph 1; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the release in ¶1; no conflicting provision located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard ADEA-compliance acknowledgment; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with ¶¶9 and 10's consideration and revocation periods; no tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed twenty-one-day consideration period; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with the OWBPA-driven structure of ¶¶8, 10 and 11; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The revocation addressees are left blank in both limbs, so the mechanics for effective revocation cannot be performed as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 11 makes the Company's obligations contingent on non-revocation and written confirmation, so the blanks here matter to the severance trigger in 8.4; the gap is a blank rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The Company's obligations" is unqualified — it does not say whether it means only severance (as the heading suggests) or every obligation under the Release — and the heading and text therefore pull apart.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.4 conditions severance on "execution without revocation" of the Release but says nothing about the written confirmation this paragraph adds as a third condition, so the two conditions-precedent regimes are not identical.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional voluntariness and no-reliance acknowledgment; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with ¶¶8, 9 and 15; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Company's half is oddly phrased — "agrees to disclose the terms of this Agreement only for legitimate business purposes" — and "legitimate business purposes" is undefined, an exception whose boundary is unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks 3.3 of the Employment Agreement, so the drafting at least is consistent; ¶3's promise not to disclose the terms to prospective employers overlaps with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line non-admission clause; nothing to interpret.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with recital D's "without any admission of liability"; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Regarding the matters set forth herein" is a self-referential limit on the integration, which leaves open what falls inside it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 5 preserves the Employment Agreement's continuing obligations and ¶1 refers to consideration set out in the Employment Agreement, so this integration clause plainly cannot be read literally as superseding that agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard unknown-facts waiver; clearly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforces ¶1's "known or unknown" release; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A carefully drafted Michigan choice-of-law clause excluding renvoi; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors 9.10 of the Employment Agreement, though the Release contains no venue clause corresponding to 9.15; that is a gap, not an inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A reformation-style severability clause, long but internally consistent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It takes the modify-and-enforce approach, unlike 9.2 of the Employment Agreement which simply severs; two different severability regimes coexist across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The forfeiture is triggered by violating "the terms of this Agreement" without any materiality or cure qualifier, and it releases the Company from obligations "under the Severance Agreement" — an instrument bearing no defined name anywhere in the document; the sentence also trails off with a comma.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Release is called the "Release" and severance is actually promised by Section 8.4 of the Employment Agreement, so the undefined "Severance Agreement" has to be matched to one of them; this also cuts against ¶1's carve-out preserving the Employee's claims to compel payment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A duties bullet listing advisory responsibilities with an "including... and other strategic partnership arrangements" catch-all; broad but plainly advisory in character.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1 says the Employee reports directly to the Board while this bullet has him advising the Chairman and the Board, and 2.1 makes the Schedule control over the Bylaws — consistent enough, but the reporting lines across the Schedule and 2.1 are not uniform.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bullet assigns responsibility for "Finance/Accounting/Cash Management (including Ajuba US and all subsidiaries)" with an "including" list whose reach is open, but the wording itself is intelligible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.4(a) expressly declares that consolidation, elimination or outsourcing of cash management, accounting and sales and marketing is not a material diminution, and 2.1 deems the Schedule amended in that event — so the very functions this bullet confers can be stripped without breach, a tension a court would have to resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single flat statement of reporting lines; nothing ambiguous in it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is subject to 2.1's deemed-amendment sentence and to 8.4's acknowledgment that the Employee's title may be reduced to Senior Vice President after year one, which would be hard to square with all India employees continuing to report to him.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four words, entirely definite on their own terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1 states that the Employee "shall report directly to the Board (or selected designee of the Board of Directors of the Parent)," while this Schedule says he reports to the Chairman — and 2.1 provides the Schedule controls over the Bylaws but says nothing about a conflict with 2.1 itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple quarterly attendance obligation; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with 9.14's recusal requirement and with 2.1's reporting duty without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Completion is defined by an objective "last to occur" test tied to named individuals and a dated lease, which is unusually precise; the cost figures are labelled estimates and the itemised list sums correctly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(f) describes Schedule I as setting out "the specific cost savings for each action," but this Schedule gives only operating-cost estimates and later disclaims any warranty of savings, so the bonus condition and the Schedule are not perfectly aligned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading and 2.2(f) speak of "restructure," but the text defines completion solely by termination of a named lease, and it also slips into speaking of "closure" of the Novi office — a shift of concept within one paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(f) conditions $200,000 on the Novi office being "restructured" in accordance with this Schedule, so whether lease termination alone earns the bonus depends on reading the two together; the risk-assessment sentence is also qualified by the disclaimer that follows.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear disclaimer that the figures are good-faith estimates only, though it references "Contemplated Transactions (as defined in the Stock Purchase Agreement dated June __, 2005)" — an undated, unattached instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(f) treats Schedule I as "set[ting] forth the specific cost savings for each action and a reasonable risk assessment," while this paragraph disclaims any representation as to actual savings — the operative bonus clause and the Schedule characterise the same content differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single allocation sentence, unambiguous in scope and in who bears the cost.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It places the closure costs on Ajuba even though 2.2(f) has Ajuba India paying the Reorganization Bonus and the Company as a whole benefiting; a minor allocation mismatch, not a genuine conflict.
